items.title: Improve ordering of top-level commands
items.reason: Its discussion explicitly grouped seven proposed commands as workspace operations, but the accepted outcome was top-level ordering, not a `uv workspace` hierarchy.

items.title: Improve display order of top-level commands
items.reason: This implemented astral-sh/uv#5702 by reordering top-level commands; it addressed similar discoverability concerns without adding workspace aliases.

items.title: Missing documentation for uv workspace commands
items.reason: This adjacent request concerns documenting the existing workspace inspection namespace, not aliases for project-management commands.

related.search_scope: Searched issues and pull requests for each proposed workspace form: init, add, remove, sync, lock, run, tree, build, and publish. Conceptual searches covered workspace commands, subcommands, aliases, namespaces, CLI grouping, project namespaces, and monorepo tooling. Inspected candidate discussions and references. Astral-sh/uv#9626 concerns affected-package builds and versioning; astral-sh/uv#12541 and astral-sh/uv#13636 concern specific inspection commands. Astral-sh/uv#18368 was closed without merge and does not implement these aliases.

type_reason: The issue requests a new CLI hierarchy and alias surface to improve discoverability. It reports no incorrect behavior, and the closest prior discussion only changed top-level command ordering, so no existing issue or pull request tracks the same request closely enough for duplicate classification.
summary: No duplicate was found. Astral-sh/uv#5702 and astral-sh/uv#5830 are the closest precedent but retained top-level commands; astral-sh/uv#18215 only concerns documentation for existing inspection commands.
draft_response:
Thanks for the proposal. The existing project commands already operate in workspace contexts, while `uv workspace` currently exposes workspace inspection commands. The closest prior CLI discussion, astral-sh/uv#5702, grouped many of these commands conceptually as workspace operations, but astral-sh/uv#5830 addressed discoverability by ordering the top-level commands rather than nesting or aliasing them.

We’ll treat this as an enhancement proposal. Adding aliases for the full set would need design consensus, particularly because commands such as `init`, `add`, `remove`, `run`, `build`, and `publish` can target a project or member rather than the workspace as a whole. Concrete examples where the current commands are unclear, along with the expected whole-workspace versus member-specific behavior for each proposed command, would help define the design.
